items.title: Trump lands in China for trade talks, Xi summit
items.feedTitle: Trump lands in China for trade talks and high-stakes summit with Xi and Putin
items.summary: President Trump arrived in Shenzhen, China, after signing a trade deal and pledging defense cooperation with the Philippines. He is scheduled to hold a historic trilateral summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday at the APEC summit. The meeting marks a rare diplomatic moment as Trump begins his administration's engagement with major global powers.

items.title: Four Maryland students sue over AI false gun detection
items.feedTitle: Four Maryland high school students sue after AI mistakes Doritos bag for gun
items.summary: Four Black high school students filed a lawsuit after an AI system mistakenly identified a Doritos bag as a firearm, leading to their detention and search. The misidentification by the artificial intelligence system raised serious concerns about algorithmic bias and racial profiling in security systems. The incident highlights ongoing problems with AI accuracy in real-world law enforcement applications.

items.title: Man sentenced to 27 years for Iran-backed Trump plot
items.feedTitle: Man sentenced to 27 years in prison over foiled plot to kill Trump
items.summary: A Pakistani national was sentenced to over 27 years in prison for his role in an alleged assassination plot targeting President Trump, which authorities say was directed from Iran. The case represents one of the most serious security threats against the sitting president in recent years. The conviction underscores ongoing concerns about potential Iranian-backed operations targeting US leadership.

items.title: Muslims to outnumber Christians by 2035 globally
items.feedTitle: Muslims are projected to outnumber Christians by 2035 as the world's largest religion
items.summary: According to new projections from the Pew Research Center, Islam is expected to surpass Christianity as the world's largest religion by 2035. The shift reflects faster population growth rates among Muslims compared to Christians globally. The demographic change has significant implications for global religious influence and geopolitics in the coming decades.

items.title: White House overstates credit for overdose death decline
items.feedTitle: As overdose deaths fall, White House makes misleading claims about who deserves credit
items.summary: The White House claimed credit for a historic drop in drug overdose deaths, but NPR's investigation found the biggest progress occurred under the Biden administration, not since Trump took office. The mischaracterization appears designed to boost the current administration's public health narrative. The factual discrepancy raises questions about how credit for public health achievements is being allocated.

stlouis.title: Missouri SNAP recipients drop by 41,000
stlouis.feedTitle: More than 41,000 fewer Missourians receive SNAP
stlouis.summary: More than 41,000 Missourians have lost access to SNAP food benefits in a sharp decline. The drop reflects the Trump administration's sweeping changes to work requirements for the food aid program. The loss of benefits is forcing vulnerable populations to find alternative sources of assistance amid rising living costs.

stlouis.title: St. Louis doctors warn US loses measles elimination status
stlouis.feedTitle: St. Louis doctors sound alarm after US loses measles elimination status
stlouis.summary: St. Louis-area physicians have sounded an alarm after the United States formally lost its measles elimination status this month. The loss marks a 26-year reversal in public health achievement and reflects declining vaccination rates across the country. Medical professionals in the region are calling for urgent efforts to restore immunization coverage.

stlouis.title: MetroLink extension to airport opens November 30
stlouis.feedTitle: MetroLink extension to MidAmerica St. Louis Airport gets opening date
stlouis.summary: The MetroLink extension to MidAmerica St. Louis Airport is set to begin service on November 30, 2026, providing direct rail access to the airport for the first time. The project is expected to improve transportation connectivity and potentially boost economic activity in the region. The opening date represents a milestone in St. Louis area infrastructure development.

items.title: Xi greets Trump and Putin at APEC summit
items.feedTitle: China’s Xi greets Putin and Trump at APEC before historic summit
items.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping greeted Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, setting the stage for a historic first trilateral meeting among the three leaders. The summit brings together the heads of the world's three largest military and economic powers for high-stakes discussions. The gathering represents a rare diplomatic moment as geopolitical tensions remain elevated.

items.title: ICJ to rule on Myanmar genocide case against Rohingya
items.feedTitle: ICJ to rule on Rohingya genocide case against Myanmar
items.summary: The International Court of Justice is set to issue a historic verdict on whether Myanmar committed genocide during its 2017 military crackdown that displaced at least 730,000 Rohingya. The Gambia brought the case accusing Myanmar of systematic persecution. If found guilty, Myanmar would become the first state ever convicted of genocide by an international court.

items.title: Van Gogh painting sells for record $190.4 million
items.feedTitle: Van Gogh painting sells for record $190.4m after row over its Nazi history
items.summary: A Vincent van Gogh painting from 1890 sold at auction for a record $190.4 million, but the sale was accompanied by controversy over the artwork's Nazi-era history. The painting's provenance raised questions about how the art market handles pieces with complicated historical backgrounds. Art recovery lawyers have highlighted the broader issue of overlooked historical injustices in the auction world.

items.title: Crimea bridge attacked again by Ukraine forces
items.feedTitle: Crimea bridge has been attacked again, says Russian-installed governor
items.summary: The bridge connecting Crimea to Russia across the Kerch Strait has been attacked again, marking the third assault in recent days according to Russian-appointed regional officials. Assessment of damage is underway following the latest strike. The attacks highlight Ukraine's continued efforts to disrupt Russian logistics and military supply lines to occupied territories.

items.title: Waymo suspends driverless taxis on US freeways
items.feedTitle: Waymo pulls driverless taxis from freeways across the US after California ban
items.summary: Autonomous vehicle company Waymo has temporarily pulled all its driverless robotaxis from US freeways indefinitely following a California state ban and several traffic incidents. The vehicles had been operating in 15 US cities, though freeway service was limited to a few locations. The suspension represents a significant setback for the autonomous driving industry's expansion plans.

items.title: Muslims to outnumber Christians by 2035 worldwide
items.feedTitle: Muslims to outnumber Christians by 2035 worldwide: Pew research
items.summary: According to Pew Research projections, while Muslims will become the world's largest religion by 2035, India will remain predominantly Hindu. The absolute number of Hindus in India and globally is expected to rise from 1.2 billion in 2020 to 1.4 billion by 2070. India's Muslim population will grow faster but remain a minority in the country.

items.title: India-US trade deal signing hinges on US tariff plans
items.feedTitle: Trade deal to be signed after US ready with tariff structure
items.summary: India and the US trade deal negotiations are set to wrap up soon, but the signing depends on the Trump administration finalizing its new tariff framework. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal indicated the process will take additional time as Washington develops its tariff structure. The delay reflects ongoing uncertainty about US trade policy direction.

items.title: Cyclone Akvan approaching Indian coast by November 20
items.feedTitle: Cyclone 'Akvan' updates: Akvan likely to cross between Machilipatnam and Puri, says APSDMA
items.summary: Cyclone Akvan has intensified into a severe storm and is likely to cross between Machilipatnam and Puri on the Indian coast by November 20. The storm was approximately 580 km from Visakhapatnam as of the latest update. Authorities in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha are on alert with evacuation preparations underway.

items.title: Muhammad Yunus's ancestral home set on fire
items.feedTitle: Muhammad Yunus’s ancestral home set on fire in Chattogram
items.summary: Muhammad Yunus's ancestral home in Chattogram, Bangladesh was set ablaze amid ongoing violence in the country. The incident coincides with reports of potential escalating unrest as authorities deal with security challenges. The attack on the Nobel laureate's property highlights the volatile political situation in Bangladesh.

items.title: Shiv Sena members tear Sonia Gandhi book over Savarkar
items.feedTitle: Shiv Sena members tear pages of Sonia Gandhi’s book over Savarkar references, seek ban in Maharashtra
items.summary: Shiv Sena members tore pages from Sonia Gandhi's memoir in protest over references to historical figure Savarkar and have called for a ban on the book in Maharashtra. The incident reflects ongoing political tensions over historical narratives and national identity issues. The controversy highlights deeper ideological divisions within Indian politics.

immigration.title: Labor Dept. proposes major green card hiring overhaul
immigration.feedTitle: Trump Administration Proposes First Major Green Card Hiring Overhaul in Nearly 20 Years: ‘American Workers Are First In Line’
immigration.summary: The Trump administration's Department of Labor has proposed sweeping changes to the PERM (Permanent Employment-based Residency Sponsorship) labor certification process, the first major overhaul in nearly 20 years. The proposed rule tightens standards for employer sponsorship of foreign workers and strengthens protections for US workers. This is a proposed rule, not yet finalized; the 30-day comment period will determine its final form.

immigration.title: H-1B visa holders' children get permanent residency path
immigration.feedTitle: H-1B Visa Holders’ Children Could Get Path To Permanent Residency Under Proposed Bill
immigration.summary: A proposed bill would provide H-1B visa holders' children with a pathway to permanent residency under proposed legislation being discussed in Congress. Democrats are seeking early action on the immigration bill as the new congressional session begins. This is a proposed measure, not yet enacted; its passage remains uncertain.

immigration.title: H-1B visa issuances to Indians drop 88% in one month
immigration.feedTitle: H-1B visa issuances to Indians drop 88% in a single month as appointment crisis bites
immigration.summary: H-1B visa issuances to Indian nationals have plummeted 88% in a single month as a visa appointment crisis continues to impact skilled worker admissions. H-4 visas (issued to H-1B holders' families) dropped 91% in the same period. The dramatic decline reflects ongoing processing delays and staffing constraints at USCIS affecting Indian professionals seeking US work authorization.

items.title: Anthropic prices record IPO at $83 per share
items.feedTitle: AI giant Anthropic valued at up to $1.5tn ahead of stock market debut
items.summary: Artificial intelligence company Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, raising $81.3 billion in the largest public offering on record, surpassing even SpaceX's valuation. The pricing was above the expected range, signaling strong investor enthusiasm for AI stocks despite broader market uncertainty. The company is now valued at approximately $1.5 trillion, positioning it among the world's most valuable corporations.

items.title: Fed officials worry AI bubble could shake financial system
items.feedTitle: Fed officials worry an AI bust could shake the financial system
items.summary: Federal Reserve officials expressed concerns that an AI industry downturn could pose risks to financial stability, according to meeting minutes released Wednesday. The Fed's concerns stem from massive capital investments flowing into AI infrastructure and the potential for a bubble similar to past tech crashes. Some Fed policymakers worry that unrealistic expectations could lead to severe market corrections.

items.title: India studies tax tweaks to boost stock trading activity
items.feedTitle: India Studies Tax Proposals to Encourage Stock Trading, Curb Speculative Bets
items.summary: India is weighing tax proposals to encourage stock trading while curbing speculative derivatives activity, according to Bloomberg. Market participants are seeking reductions in capital gains and transaction taxes in the upcoming Budget for FY28. The government is also considering higher derivatives taxes as part of efforts to shift trading patterns toward equities.

items.title: Nvidia board says it will not reinstate Jensen Huang
items.feedTitle: Nvidia doubles revenue as board says it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang
items.summary: Nvidia's board chairman Harvey Jones stated the company "does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO" during the company's first earnings report since the founder's unexpected ouster. Huang resigned following allegations of an affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence operative. The board's firm stance suggests a permanent leadership change despite widespread calls from tech executives and investors for his return.

finance.note: Oil prices have steadied as supply surpluses offset Middle East tensions, while the S&P 500 posted its fifth consecutive daily decline amid Fed rate-hike signals and AI bubble concerns. Nvidia shares reversed earlier gains following the company's board statement that Jensen Huang will not be reinstated as CEO. Watch: Anthropic's trading debut Thursday following its record $81.3B IPO; further Fed commentary on rate trajectory; and whether market support holds above key technical levels.

cards.title: Screen Time & Achievement Gap
cards.insight: Research shows that locking up student cellphones during class narrows the achievement gap, suggesting digital distraction disproportionately affects lower-performing students. When all students face the same focus constraints, learning outcomes become more equitable.
cards.takeaway: Consider phone-free study blocks to level the academic playing field, especially for struggling learners.

cards.title: Work-Life Rebalance for Older Adults
cards.insight: New SNAP work rules requiring people up to age 65 to work or volunteer are disrupting retirement plans for those who previously stepped back from employment to care for family. The policy shift forces difficult choices between caregiving and benefits access.
cards.takeaway: Review social safety-net eligibility requirements if you're managing elder or family care responsibilities.

cards.title: Heating Costs & Winter Health
cards.insight: Rising heating oil prices are forcing millions of US homeowners to cut back on winter warmth, with some families reporting they're often cold in their own homes. Inadequate heating increases risk of hypothermia, cardiovascular strain, and respiratory illness, especially in older adults.
cards.takeaway: Identify low-cost or no-cost heating alternatives (community warming centers, utility assistance programs) before winter peaks.

cards.title: Measles Resurgence & Vaccination Gaps
cards.insight: The US has lost its 26-year measles elimination status as vaccination rates declined; Pennsylvania alone recorded its eighth measles death of 2026. Unvaccinated individuals face severe disease risk, with complications including encephalitis and permanent disability.
cards.takeaway: Confirm measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccination status for yourself and dependents; check with your provider if unsure.

ai.title: Anthropic raises $81.3 billion in record IPO debut
ai.feedTitle: Anthropic raises $81.3bn in biggest IPO of all time
ai.summary: AI company Anthropic completed the largest initial public offering of all time, raising $81.3 billion and pricing shares at $83 each, above the expected range. The blockbuster IPO values the five-year-old firm at approximately $1.5 trillion, making it one of the most valuable US corporations. The successful offering signals strong investor appetite for AI stocks despite concerns about valuation and market saturation.

ai.title: Google rolls out Gemini 4 Neon AI model
ai.feedTitle: Google rolls out Gemini 4 Neon AI model for coding, science
ai.summary: Google has released Gemini 4 Neon, an AI model designed for coding and scientific tasks targeted at power users. The new model represents Google's efforts to compete in the rapidly evolving AI market dominated by OpenAI and Anthropic. The release marks Google's continued push to deliver advanced AI capabilities across different specialized domains.

ai.title: Governor Newsom proposes AI kill switch for releases
ai.feedTitle: Newsom touts an AI kill switch to halt dangerous OpenAI, Anthropic releases
ai.summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom has proposed an AI kill switch mechanism that would allow authorities to halt dangerous releases from companies like OpenAI and Anthropic. The proposal aims to give regulators emergency powers to prevent potentially harmful AI systems from reaching the public. This is a proposed policy measure, not yet enacted; its feasibility and legal standing remain unclear.

ai.title: New legal framework maps AI accountability boundaries
ai.feedTitle: Who's to blame for a rogue AI? New legal framework maps accountability
ai.summary: Researchers have developed a new legal framework designed to clarify accountability when rogue AI systems cause harm or behave unexpectedly. The framework addresses the complex question of who bears responsibility—developers, deployers, users, or regulators—for AI-related incidents. The work aims to guide policymakers and courts as AI liability law continues to evolve.

ai.title: Trump administration weighs requiring US AI disclosure
ai.feedTitle: EXCLUSIVE: Trump administration weighs forcing US firms to disclose Chinese AI use
ai.summary: The Trump administration is considering requiring US companies to disclose their use of Chinese artificial intelligence systems, according to exclusive reporting. The proposal reflects concerns about technology transfer and national security risks from American firms relying on Chinese AI capabilities. The measure is under consideration but not yet finalized.
